import pytest

from planner.model import Section
from planner.show import active_days, render


def row(course, section, day, start, end, location="R"):
    return Section(course, section, day, start * 60, end * 60, location)


def test_empty_grid():
    assert render([]) == "(no meetings)\n"


def test_header_lists_only_days_with_meetings():
    rows = [row("A", "1", "Wed", 9, 10), row("B", "1", "Mon", 9, 10)]
    out = render(rows)
    header = out.splitlines()[0]
    assert header.split() == ["Mon", "Wed"]
    assert "A 1" in out and "09:00-10:00" in out


def test_active_days_order():
    rows = [row("A", "1", "Fri", 9, 10), row("B", "1", "Mon", 9, 10)]
    assert active_days(rows) == ["Mon", "Fri"]


def test_days_argument_forces_columns():
    out = render([row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10)], days=["Mon", "Tue"])
    assert out.splitlines()[0].split() == ["Mon", "Tue"]


def test_hour_window_hides_meetings():
    rows = [row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10, "R1"), row("B", "1", "Mon", 15, 16, "R2")]
    out = render(rows, start=14 * 60, end=17 * 60)
    assert "B 1" in out and "A 1" not in out
    assert out.splitlines()[-3].startswith("17:00") is False
    lines = out.splitlines()
    assert any(line.startswith("14:00") for line in lines)
    assert any(line.startswith("16:00") for line in lines)


def test_meeting_overlapping_window_start_is_shown_clipped():
    meeting = Section("A", "1", "Mon", 9 * 60 + 30, 10 * 60 + 30, "R")
    out = render([meeting], start=10 * 60, end=11 * 60)
    assert "10:00-10:30" in out
    assert "A 1" in out
    assert any(line.startswith("10:00|") for line in out.splitlines())
    assert not any(line.startswith("09:00|") for line in out.splitlines())


def test_two_meetings_in_same_hour_share_a_cell():
    rows = [row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10, "X"), row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10, "Y")]
    out = render(rows)
    assert "X" in out and "Y" in out


def test_grid_width_is_bounded():
    out = render([row("LONGC", "99", "Mon", 9, 10, "VeryLongRoomName")], width=12)
    for line in out.splitlines():
        assert len(line) <= 7 + 13


def test_invalid_arguments():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="at least 12"):
        render([row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10)], width=5)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="unknown day"):
        render([row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10)], days=["Funday"])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="start must be before"):
        render([row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10)], start=600, end=600)

import pytest

from planner.model import PlannerError, Section
from planner.solver import Choice, group_sections, overlaps, solve


def row(course, section, day, start, end, location="R"):
    return Section(course, section, day, start * 60, end * 60, location)


DATA = [
    row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10),
    row("A", "2", "Tue", 9, 10),
    row("B", "1", "Mon", 9, 10),
    row("B", "2", "Mon", 11, 12),
    row("B", "2", "Tue", 14, 15),  # second meeting of the same section
]


def test_group_sections_merges_meetings():
    groups = group_sections(DATA)
    assert list(groups) == ["A", "B"]
    assert [(g.section, len(g.meetings)) for g in groups["B"]] == [("1", 1), ("2", 2)]


def test_overlaps_touching_is_not_overlap():
    assert overlaps([row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10)], [row("B", "1", "Mon", 10, 11)]) is False
    assert overlaps([row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10)], [row("B", "1", "Mon", 9, 30)]) is True
    assert overlaps([row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10)], [row("B", "1", "Tue", 9, 10)]) is False


def test_solve_returns_all_feasible_schedules_in_file_order():
    schedules = solve(DATA, ["A", "B"])
    pairs = [(c[0].section, c[1].section) for c in schedules]
    # B 2 meets on Mon 11-12 and Tue 14-15, so it fits next to every A
    # section; A 1 and B 1 clash on Mon 09-10, and so do A 2 and B 2's Mon
    # meeting is 11-12 so it does not. All three combinations are feasible.
    assert pairs == [("1", "2"), ("2", "1"), ("2", "2")]


def test_solve_limit():
    assert len(solve(DATA, ["A", "B"], limit=1)) == 1


def test_section_with_two_meetings_must_fit_on_both_days():
    schedules = solve(DATA, ["B", "A"])
    assert [(c[0].section, c[1].section) for c in schedules] == [
        ("1", "2"),
        ("2", "1"),
        ("2", "2"),
    ]
    two = schedules[1][0]
    assert isinstance(two, Choice)
    assert [m.day for m in two.meetings] == ["Mon", "Tue"]  # both meetings kept
    assert two.places() == ["R", "R"]
    assert "Mon " in two_label(two) and "Tue " in two_label(two)


def two_label(choice):
    from planner.solver import describe

    return describe(choice)


def test_unknown_course_message():
    with pytest.raises(PlannerError, match=r"unknown course\(s\): Z \(known courses: A, B\)"):
        solve(DATA, ["Z"])


def test_duplicate_course_request():
    with pytest.raises(PlannerError, match="more than once"):
        solve(DATA, ["A", "A"])


def test_no_courses():
    with pytest.raises(PlannerError, match="no courses"):
        solve(DATA, [])


def test_course_with_internal_clash_is_rejected():
    data = DATA + [row("C", "1", "Fri", 9, 10), row("C", "1", "Fri", 9, 30, "S")]
    with pytest.raises(PlannerError, match="course C is unusable"):
        solve(data, ["C"])


def test_skips_internally_clashing_section_if_another_is_usable():
    data = [
        Section("C", "1", "Mon", 9 * 60, 10 * 60, "R"),
        Section("C", "1", "Mon", 9 * 60 + 30, 10 * 60 + 30, "S"),
        Section("C", "2", "Tue", 9 * 60, 10 * 60, "T"),
    ]
    schedules = solve(data, ["C"])
    assert len(schedules) == 1
    assert schedules[0][0].section == "2"


def test_impossible_explanation_names_the_pair():
    data = [row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10), row("B", "1", "Mon", 9, 30, 10)]
    with pytest.raises(PlannerError) as info:
        solve(data, ["A", "B"])
    assert "A and B cannot be combined at all" in str(info.value)


def test_explanation_names_the_most_constrained_course():
    # Pairwise feasible, but A and C together leave B no slot. B is the most
    # constrained course, so its sections are reported.
    data = [
        row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10),
        row("B", "1", "Mon", 9, 10),
        row("B", "2", "Mon", 11, 12),
        row("C", "1", "Mon", 11, 12),
    ]
    for pair in (["A", "B"], ["A", "C"], ["B", "C"]):
        assert solve(data, pair)
    with pytest.raises(PlannerError) as info:
        solve(data, ["A", "B", "C"])
    message = str(info.value)
    assert message.startswith("no schedule without overlaps is possible for A, B, C")
    assert "for example" in message
    assert "Mon 09:00-10:00 in R" in message
    assert "clashes with" in message
    # the message must point at a course whose sections cannot all be used
    assert "A 1" in message or "B 1" in message or "C 1" in message


def test_impossible_due_to_combination_not_pair():
    # Every pair of courses can be combined, but not all three together:
    # A's Monday section clashes with B, its Tuesday section with C.
    data = [
        row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10),
        row("A", "2", "Tue", 9, 10),
        row("B", "1", "Mon", 9, 10),
        row("C", "1", "Tue", 9, 10),
    ]
    for pair in (["A", "B"], ["A", "C"], ["B", "C"]):
        assert solve(data, pair)
    with pytest.raises(PlannerError) as info:
        solve(data, ["A", "B", "C"])
    message = str(info.value)
    assert "no schedule without overlaps is possible" in message
    # The explanation must not claim a pair is hopeless: (A, B) is feasible.
    assert "cannot be combined at all" not in message


def test_explanation_falls_back_when_no_course_looks_constrained():
    # A and B are each available, but B's only section clashes with C's only
    # section, so the pair message is used and no "for example" is invented.
    from planner.solver import Choice, _explain_impossible

    options = [
        [Choice("A", "1", [row("A", "1", "Mon", 9, 10)])],
        [
            Choice("B", "1", [row("B", "1", "Mon", 9, 10)]),
            Choice("B", "2", [row("B", "2", "Mon", 9, 10)]),
        ],
    ]
    # force the "available" branch of the per-course explanation
    text = _explain_impossible(["A", "B"], options)
    assert "cannot be combined at all" in text

"""Tests for the M2 preference ranking search."""

import itertools
import random

import pytest

from planner.model import PlannerError, Section
from planner.preferences import lesson_key, measure
from planner.ranking import search
from planner.solver import solve

ORDER = ("days", "early", "gaps", "span")


def section(course, sec, day, start, end, location="Room"):
    return Section(course, sec, day, start * 60, end * 60, location)


def exact_key(choices, order=ORDER, not_before=9 * 60):
    meetings = [row for choice in choices for row in choice.meetings]
    return (
        measure(meetings, not_before=not_before).as_tuple(order),
        [(choice.course, choice.section) for choice in choices],
        lesson_key(meetings),
    )


def brute_force(rows, courses, order=ORDER, not_before=9 * 60):
    return [exact_key(item, order, not_before) for item in sorted(
        (list(schedule) for schedule in solve(rows, courses)),
        key=lambda item: exact_key(item, order, not_before),
    )]


def random_instance(rng, courses_max=4):
    rows, courses = [], []
    for index in range(rng.randint(2, courses_max)):
        name = f"C{index}"
        courses.append(name)
        for sec in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            for day in rng.sample(["Mon", "Tue", "Wed"], rng.randint(1, 2)):
                start = rng.randrange(8, 14)
                rows.append(section(name, f"S{sec}", day, start, start + rng.choice([1, 1.5]) and start + 1
                                    if False else start + 1))
    return rows, courses


def test_returns_best_schedule_first():
    rows = [
        section("A", "S0", "Mon", 8, 9),
        section("A", "S1", "Mon", 10, 11),
        section("B", "S0", "Mon", 11, 12),
        section("B", "S1", "Tue", 9, 10),
    ]
    result = search(rows, ["A", "B"], not_before=9 * 60)
    assert result.complete is True
    assert result.total == 3
    best = result.best[0]
    # Two days for A=S0,B=S1 vs one day for A=S1,B=S0: fewest days wins.
    assert [c.section for c in best.choices] == ["S1", "S0"]
    assert best.metrics.days == 1
    assert [item.rank for item in result.best] == [1, 2, 3]


def test_limit_is_respected():
    rows = [
        section("A", "S0", "Mon", 9, 10),
        section("A", "S1", "Tue", 9, 10),
        section("B", "S0", "Wed", 9, 10),
        section("B", "S1", "Thu", 9, 10),
    ]
    result = search(rows, ["A", "B"], limit=2)
    assert len(result.best) == 2
    assert result.total == 4


def test_matches_brute_force_on_random_instances():
    rng = random.Random(2024)
    checked = 0
    for _ in range(150):
        rows, courses = random_instance(rng)
        try:
            expected = brute_force(rows, courses)[:5]
        except PlannerError:
            with pytest.raises(PlannerError):
                search(rows, courses, limit=5)
            continue
        result = search(rows, courses, limit=5)
        assert [exact_key(item.choices) for item in result.best] == expected
        assert result.complete is True
        assert result.total == len(brute_force(rows, courses))
        checked += 1
    assert checked > 30


def test_matches_brute_force_with_other_orders():
    rows = [
        section("A", "S0", "Mon", 8, 9),
        section("A", "S1", "Mon", 9, 10),
        section("B", "S0", "Mon", 9, 10),
        section("B", "S1", "Tue", 13, 14),
        section("C", "S0", "Wed", 10, 11),
        section("C", "S1", "Mon", 11, 12),
    ]
    for order in itertools.permutations(ORDER):
        expected = [
            exact_key(item, order)[:2]
            for item in brute_force(rows, ["A", "B", "C"], order=order)
        ]
        result = search(rows, ["A", "B", "C"], order=list(order))
        assert [exact_key(item.choices, order)[:2] for item in result.best] == expected, order


def test_patience_reports_incomplete_but_keeps_best_found():
    # 8 courses with 3 sections each on distinct slots would be 3**8 = 6561
    # schedules; a patience of 200 cuts the count short.
    rows = []
    for course in range(8):
        for sec in range(3):
            rows.append(section(f"C{course}", f"S{sec}", "Mon", 8 + course, 9 + course))
    result = search(rows, [f"C{course}" for course in range(8)], limit=3, patience=200)
    assert result.complete is False
    assert result.explored <= 200
    assert len(result.best) == 3
    # The patience cap must not corrupt the top list.
    everything = search(rows, [f"C{course}" for course in range(8)], limit=3, patience=10**6)
    assert [exact_key(i.choices)[:2] for i in result.best] == [
        exact_key(i.choices)[:2] for i in everything.best
    ]


def test_single_feasible_schedule():
    rows = [section("A", "S0", "Mon", 9, 10), section("B", "S0", "Tue", 9, 10)]
    result = search(rows, ["A", "B"])
    assert result.total == 1
    assert len(result.best) == 1


def test_impossible_raises_clear_error():
    rows = [section("A", "S0", "Mon", 9, 10), section("B", "S0", "Mon", 9, 10)]
    with pytest.raises(PlannerError, match="no schedule without overlaps"):
        search(rows, ["A", "B"])


def test_duplicate_and_unknown_courses():
    rows = [section("A", "S0", "Mon", 9, 10)]
    with pytest.raises(PlannerError, match="more than once"):
        search(rows, ["A", "A"])
    with pytest.raises(PlannerError, match="unknown course"):
        search(rows, ["A", "B"])


def test_bad_limit():
    rows = [section("A", "S0", "Mon", 9, 10)]
    with pytest.raises(PlannerError, match="max_results"):
        search(rows, ["A"], limit=0)

"""M2 benchmark: rank 40 courses x 5 sections in well under two seconds.

Builds the timetable from ``tests/make_bench.py`` (deterministic), runs the
real CLI ``planner plan ... --top 10`` on it two ways, and fails with a
non-zero exit code if any run takes 2 seconds or more.

Usage: ``python tests/benchmark.py [--json]``
"""

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))

import make_bench  # noqa: E402  (needs the path tweak above)

BUDGET_SECONDS = 2.0
LIMIT = 10

CASES = {
    "default order": ["--top", str(LIMIT)],
    "days, gaps, span": [
        "--top", str(LIMIT), "--prefer", "days", "--prefer", "gaps", "--prefer", "span",
        "--not-before", "09:00",
    ],
}


def run_cli(data: Path, courses: list[str], options: list[str]) -> float:
    command = [sys.executable, "-m", "planner", "plan", str(data), *courses, *options]
    started = time.perf_counter()
    completed = subprocess.run(
        command, cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120
    )
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
    if completed.returncode != 0:
        raise SystemExit(
            "benchmark command failed:\n"
            + " ".join(command)
            + "\n"
            + completed.stderr
        )
    if not completed.stdout.strip():
        raise SystemExit("benchmark command printed nothing")
    return elapsed


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print machine-readable results")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    data = make_bench.write()
    courses = sorted({row[0] for row in make_bench.generate()})
    print(f"benchmark data: {data} ({len(courses)} courses x {make_bench.SECTIONS_PER_COURSE} sections)")

    results = {}
    failures = []
    for label, options in CASES.items():
        elapsed = run_cli(data, courses, options)
        results[label] = round(elapsed, 3)
        status = "ok" if elapsed < BUDGET_SECONDS else "TOO SLOW"
        print(f"  {label:<18} {elapsed:6.3f}s  (budget {BUDGET_SECONDS:.0f}s)  {status}")
        if elapsed >= BUDGET_SECONDS:
            failures.append(label)

    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps(results))
    if failures:
        print("benchmark FAILED for: " + ", ".join(failures))
        return 1
    print("benchmark passed")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Ensure development dependencies are installed
if ! python3 -c "import pytest, pytest_cov, icalendar" &>/dev/null; then
    echo "Installing dev dependencies from requirements-dev.txt..."
    python3 -m pip install -q --user -r requirements-dev.txt
fi

echo "=== Running test suite with coverage ==="
python3 -m pytest -v --cov=planner --cov-fail-under=90 "$@"

# Run benchmark if present
for bench in benchmark.py benchmarks/benchmark.py tests/benchmark.py benchmarks/bench.py; do
    if [[ -f "$bench" ]]; then
        echo "=== Running benchmark ($bench) ==="
        python3 "$bench"
        break
    fi
done

echo "=== All checks passed! ==="
